observations.seen: Frame 2 (clouds) is overexposed and low-contrast; the lavender-white platforms and pale sky merge into one flat value range with no visible key-light direction.
Frame 3 is lit in a single orange-brown hue against a flat dark brown backdrop, so the subject has no rim or fill separation from the beige floor.
In frame 1 the forest grass reads evenly lit and the trees are flat-shaded per face; the sun direction is only weakly legible.
Frame 1 grass shows large blocky, stair-stepped shadow-map texels, and the character's contact shadow is a pixelated smear.
In frame 2 the character's shadow on the platform is a clearly aliased pixel block, detached and offset from the feet.
Frame 4 has a glossy purple floor with plausible reflections and chrome rings picking up highlights. The frame 2 platforms and frame 1 grass show no environment response and look matte and unlit-ish.

Every world is a single straight lane of floating rectangular slabs in an empty void. Set dressing is sparse: a few rocks, two towers, two rings. Frame 3 has no sky or distant geometry, only a brown wall.
Frames 1 and 2 have distance haze and frame 4 has drifting sparkles, but frame 3 has no depth fog, so the background towers sit at the same value as the foreground.

Platforms are untextured slabs in grey-lavender (frame 2) and beige (frame 3) with uniform roughness, and the frame 1 grass is a stretched, smeared green texture. The acorn character's cap and skin read well by comparison.

Asset styles clash: flat low-poly pine trees and bare trunks in frame 1 sit next to high-detail scanned-looking rocks, ornate gates and kitbashed purple drones, while the platforms are simple bevelled boxes.

All four frames use a symmetric center-lane layout with the character at about 10–15% of frame height. The lower 40% of each frame is empty floor, and the goal structures are tiny at the vanishing point.
The camera follows from low and directly behind the character rather than from the expected side-on angle, so most of the frame is ground plane and jump distances are hard to read.
Frame 2 has a heavy blurred blob across the bottom foreground from depth of field. Tone mapping is washed out in frame 2 and muddy in frame 3. Bloom in frame 4 is acceptable.

The frame 1 HUD pills (hearts, world, sun-seeds, acorns, time) are clean and use a consistent warm cream style, but the top debug-style world-select bar and the small low-contrast text compete with the gameplay HUD.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
